    Structured data
    13,286

    One template put disallowed schema on every page

    I traced a product-style rating block to one byte-identical template on 677 of 679 core pages and every blog post, in all 13 languages. Engineering removed it in two releases and I verified both.

    1. SignalRating and pricing markup Google doesn’t allow on those pages
    2. Fix4,511 blog pages on 4 May, 8,775 core pages on 14 July
    3. Proof646-page staging crawl, then production checks
    Page speed · mobile homepage
    33May
    91July

    PageSpeed performance from 33 to 91

    Largest Contentful Paint, before13.4 s
    After2.9 s
    1. CauseRender-blocking CSS and hydration on the homepage
    2. ResultBlocking time 630 → 170 ms; best practices 81 → 96
    3. NextTap response traced to a synchronous analytics chain in the trial button
    Crawl coverage
    1,052 of 187,000

    The audit that lost 186,000 URLs

    Coverage collapsed. I proved it was caps inside the tool, not the site, before anyone started fixing the wrong thing. Then I rebuilt the audit to cover everything.

    1. FixAudit raised from 10K to 50K pages and from 1 to 48 hours
    2. FoundA 19,124-URL rendered crawl showed hreflang duplication on 95.89% of URLs
    3. NowAbout 28,900 URLs read every day
    Recovery
    598 URLs

    Bringing pruned content back, and proving it worked

    After 61 blog posts were pruned in one release, their traffic didn’t carry over. I restored 46 of them in four batches and measured each against a control group of 20 untouched sections.

    1. ChecksEvery URL: 200, no redirect hops, self-canonical, no noindex, 14 hreflang tags, in sitemap
    2. ResultThe first batch passed its baseline clicks on day 4
    3. AlsoIsolated a Thai-only indexing lag by ruling out content, markup and serving
    Site architecture · 3D model

    03AI search

    Getting a brand cited by AI assistants

    I built respond.io’s AI-search program from zero. A page has to be crawled, rendered, understood and retrieved before an assistant will cite it, so I work every stage.

    Stage 01 / 05Crawl
    1. 01
      User-agent: GPTBot
      Allow: /blog/
      Disallow: /cdn-cgi/

      Crawl

      Cloudflare rules and robots.txt so ClaudeBot and GPTBot spend their visits on pages that matter.

      Edge rulesAI crawl budget
    2. 02
      Raw HTML
      =
      Rendered
      ✓ match

      Render

      AI crawlers don’t run JavaScript. I removed a whole-page duplication and built a post-publish check on raw HTML.

      Raw = renderedchecked after publish
    3. 03

      Understand

      One JSON-LD @graph per page, with each page’s name and description bound to its own title and meta.

      4,394blog URLs, 13 locales
    4. 04
      respond.io
      top 10

      Retrieve

      An assistant can only cite what its search layer finds. I measured how closely Claude follows Brave’s rankings.

      243queries audited
    5. 05
      [1] respond.io

      Cite & measure

      Profound with prompt-set governance, plus AI-bot visits streamed in from my Cloudflare Worker.

      513citations in the first hour
    When a page ranked in Brave’s top 10, Claude cited it about 97% of the time. Outside the top 10, it stayed silent about 75% of the time.

    My 243-query Brave–Claude citation audit, shared with the company’s AI optimization committee
